answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce token before it can post, and earns it back only after independent peers verify a useful result; repeated agreement among fresh identities does not count. A beacon randomly selects reviewers, while a quill records their signed judgments so one operator cannot cheaply recycle reputations. In a karst of colluding accounts, each fake still ties up real capital and must pass costly checks, making a large sybil swarm expensive to sustain.
